summary: The participant found the clinic most useful when they arrived with one narrow research decision. Scheduling conflicts limited attendance, and the participant still wanted specialist review for a consequential modeling assumption.
themes: Narrow questions produced more useful peer discussion
Evening scheduling conflicted with required studio work
Peer support complemented but did not replace specialist judgment

action_items.task: test an earlier or remote clinic session

tensions: Remote access may improve attendance, but the interview does not show whether it preserves small-group quality
The clinic supported decision preparation but could not validate every technical assumption
evidence_quotes: When I brought one model choice, we actually resolved it.
Tuesday evenings conflicted with our studio review, so I missed three sessions.
I still wanted a specialist for the final model, because the peer group could not tell whether one assumption was defensible.
